chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Khirash, the freedman of Anas ibn Malik, narrated to me, he said: My master Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Fasting is a shield (meaning a barrier) from the Fire. He said this because fasting is an inner act of worship in which there is no urge of the devil nor showing off by humans.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of fasting as a shield from Hellfire?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights fasting as a spiritual barrier against Hellfire, emphasizing its nature as an inner act of worship (*nasak*) that remains hidden from public view. This secrecy protects the fast from *riya* (showing off) and the devil's influence, distinguishing it from outward rituals like prayer. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual purity and sincerity inherent in voluntary acts of devotion.
